@Bianca Viray @Grant Yang @Bryan Boehnke @John Leo

Hello Mathlib Community. I am an undergraduate researcher at the University of Washington's Math AI Lab, under Professor Bianca Viray. We have a host of lemmas which are dedicated to proving the following: that an etale extension of two local rings is generated by a single element; further, if the extension is not etale, but there is a height one prime ideal such that the induced map between the quotients of the rings is etale and the rings are regular, then the extension is still generated by a single element.

The first PR we are planning to make includes the result that, for finite free modules over a nontrivial ring, the degree of the minimal polynomial of any element is bounded by the rank of the module, and the result that: If R {α} = S and S is a finite free R-module, then S ≅ R[X]/(minpoly R α) as an R-algebra. We were deliberating on whether to situate these within Mathlib/RingTheory/IsAdjoinRoot.lean, or within some other location more closely related to minpoly. In IsAdjoinRoot, we must _root_ the theorems, but there are no additional imports, yet the first result discussed maybe does not feel wholly at home in IsAdjoinRoot.

here is a draft of our PR, and we are thinking of focusing on our changes to IsAdjoinRoot.lean first:

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/compare/master...uw-math-ai:mathlib4:grant/monogenic-extensions
The minpoly result should probably go lower if it can (splitting up your lemmas across multiple files is totally fine!).
But I'd say just open the PR and see what people say
Also, if you're having to _root_ a lot of theorems, then you should probably move them out of that namespace to a different section.
Thank you very much, we will get the review process going shortly! We will try to relocate these theorems.

Hi! For the Cayley-Hamilton thing, it looks like we need to import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.Basic to use LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly, but that file transitively imports FieldTheory.Minpoly.Basic, creating an import cycle. Is it still possible to make it go through? Taking a step back, is Minpoly.Basic the right place for our theorem despite the large import changes?

We did have an old version of the proof that avoids choosing a basis, and I assume this is what you mean for the chi(x) = 0 proof instead of chi(lmul x) = 0:

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.Basic
open Polynomial
variable {R S} [CommRing R] [Ring S] [Algebra R S]

theorem Algebra.aeval_self_charpoly [Module.Free R S] [Module.Finite R S] {α : S} :
  aeval α (Algebra.lmul R S α).charpoly = 0 :=
  Algebra.lmul_injective (by
    rw [map_zero, ← aeval_algHom_apply]; exact LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly <| Algebra.lmul R S α)

theorem minpoly.natDegree_le' [Module.Finite R S]
    [Module.Free R S] [Nontrivial R] (α : S) :
    (minpoly R α).natDegree ≤ Module.finrank R S := by
  set lα := Algebra.lmul R S α
  calc (minpoly R α).natDegree
      ≤ lα.charpoly.natDegree :=
        natDegree_le_natDegree (minpoly.min R α lα.charpoly_monic Algebra.aeval_self_charpoly)
    _ = Module.finrank R S := lα.charpoly_natDegree

General advice: either move the needed lemma upstream or the new lemma downstream, depending on what is actually needed for the proof and what makes the most sense given the file structure. Sometimes this means deciding that the existing structure is bad and that some files need to be split to minimise the imports in the simpler section of the file!

And yes that proof looks like what I had in mind, thanks!
(although the set is not necessary for a short term used just twice and the calc can just be a simpa).

Hi! For the Cayley-Hamilton thing, it looks like we need to import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.Basic to use LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly, but that file transitively imports FieldTheory.Minpoly.Basic, creating an import cycle.

I have looked into whether everything was in the right place by researching the proof of docs#Algebra.IsIntegral.of_finite, because that result has the same informal proof. Turns out this uses a version of Cayley-Hamilton called docs#LinearMap.exists_monic_and_aeval_eq_zero in Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Charpoly.LinearMap, which is indeed well upstream of Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.Basic.

However it looks like that lemma isn't quite strong enough for what we want because docs#LinearMap.exists_monic_and_aeval_eq_zero is missing a bound on the polynomial degree. It should be something like p.natDegree ≤ ⊤.spanFinrank. This would require us to import docs#spanRank into Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Charpoly.LinearMap. We would get a result like (minpoly R α).natDegree ≤ ⊤.spanFinrank, which would give us what we want in the free case.

In any case your minpoly.natDegree_le' either has to use this hypothetical stronger form of docs#LinearMap.exists_monic_and_aeval_eq_zero, or (as you have done) to use docs#LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly, in which case your lemmas work fine in Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.Basic (you would then import this into Mathlib.RingTheory.IsAdjoinRoot).
Personally I think it would be great if you did this generalisation to p.natDegree ≤ ⊤.spanFinrank but I appreciate I'm asking for extra work.

For minpoly.natDegree_le', we decided to go with using  docs#LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly since we have another PR that depends on this one.

For the comment about the Orzech property refactoring: we are not sure we understand what you mean. We use minpoly.natDegree_le' to get equality of the ranks of the modules in question and then use Orzech to deduce that the map is a bijection. But it seems like you are suggesting that we use the same code to use the Orzech property to get a bound on ranks? Do you mind explaining a little bit more what you mean?

And then in your proof just use that fact and not explicit embeddings into submodules etc

The Orzech property part comes later, and I tried to write up this natural language version of our proof:

To use docs#IsAdjoinRoot.ofAdjoinRootEquiv, we wish to prove that our chosen φ is a bijection, and we already have that it is surjective.

Let A = AdjoinRoot f. First let us construct a linear equivalence e : A ≃ₗ[R] S using finrank A = finrank S. First we get finrank A <= finrank S using minpoly.natDegree_le' and finrank A = f.natDegree. The other side comes from the fact that φ : A → S is surjective. Now we need to prove that φ is injective. Consider e⁻¹ ∘ φ : A → A. Since e is a bijection and φ is surjective, e⁻¹ ∘ φ is a surjective endomorphism, so by Orzech property it is injective. Given the hypothesis φ(x) = φ(y), we have e⁻¹(φ(x)) = e⁻¹(φ(x)) and thus x = y, so φ is injective too.

OK so you don't actually want to have to talk about e at this high level, right? And indeed you shouldn't need to prove finrank S ≤ finrank A before you apply Orzech property, because you should be able to just use the embedding of a free module into a higher-rank one. Something like

theorem OrzechProperty.bijective_of_surjective_of_finrank_le
    {R M N : Type*} [Semiring R] [OrzechProperty R]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Free R M]
    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N] [Module.Free R N]
    (h : Module.finrank R M ≤ Module.finrank R N) (f : M →ₗ[R] N)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) : Function.Bijective f

Unfortunately, this embedding doesn't appear to exist in Mathlib, so we will either have to either hide e in the proof of OrzechProperty.bijective_of_surjective_of_finrank_le or define this embedding. I think we should define this embedding because that's the thing that makes it easiest for future contributors. It's just a modification of docs#Module.le_rank_iff_exists_linearMap to include the isomorphism between M and Fin n → R.
The lemma finrank_quotient_span_eq_natDegree' is also badly typed where it's used and should have an AdjoinRoot version, but that's maybe not worth fixing since ▸ works fine.
There seems to be a lot of stuff missing that should be added to Mathlib to make this proof go smoothly. I think the AdjoinRoot API is just quite old. Good motivation for me to rewrite it!

theorem exists_injective_map
    {R : Type u} {M : Type v} {N : Type w} [Semiring R] [Nontrivial R] [StrongRankCondition R]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Free R M]
    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N]
    (h : Module.finrank R M ≤ Module.rank R N) :
    ∃ f : M →ₗ[R] N, Function.Injective f := by
  rw [Module.le_rank_iff_exists_linearMap] at h
  rcases h with ⟨φ, hφ⟩
  exact ⟨φ ∘ₛₗ
      (LinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq (R := R) M (Fin (Module.finrank R M) → R) (by simp)).toLinearMap,
    by simpa⟩

theorem exists_injective_map_fin
    {R : Type u} {M : Type v} {N : Type w} [Semiring R] [Nontrivial R] [StrongRankCondition R]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Free R M]
    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (h : Module.finrank R M ≤ Module.finrank R N) :
    ∃ f : M →ₗ[R] N, Function.Injective f := exists_injective_map <| by
  rw [← Module.finrank_eq_rank R N, Nat.cast_le]
  exact h

theorem _root_.OrzechProperty.bijective_of_surjective_of_finrank_le
    {R M N : Type*} [Semiring R] [Nontrivial R] [OrzechProperty R]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Free R M]
    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N] [Module.Free R N]
    (h : Module.finrank R M ≤ Module.finrank R N) (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    Function.Bijective f := by
  rcases exists_injective_map_fin h with ⟨φ, hφ⟩
  refine OrzechProperty.bijective_of_surjective_of_injective φ _ hφ hf

Oh and by the way on this: are you aware of "spread notation"? Your proof goes around in a circle because you prove IsAdjoinRoot S (minpoly R α) inside the ker_map field, then re-compute the kernel from that. Instead you should write something like

def mkOfAdjoinEqTop'
    [Module.Finite R S] [Module.Free R S] [Nontrivial R]
    {α : S} (hα : Algebra.adjoin R {α} = ⊤) :
    IsAdjoinRootMonic S (minpoly R α) where
  __ : IsAdjoinRoot S (minpoly R α) :=
  let f := minpoly R α
  have hf := minpoly.monic (Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral (R := R) α)
  let φ : AdjoinRoot f →ₐ[R] S :=
      AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom f (Algebra.ofId R S) α (minpoly.aeval R α)
  haveI := hf.free_adjoinRoot; haveI := hf.finite_adjoinRoot
  IsAdjoinRoot.ofAdjoinRootEquiv AlgEquiv.ofBijective φ <| by
    have hφ : Function.Surjective φ := by
      rw [Algebra.adjoin_singleton_eq_range_aeval, AlgHom.range_eq_top] at hα
      intro s; obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hα s
      exact ⟨AdjoinRoot.mk f p, by simp [φ, ← aeval_def, hp]⟩
    sorry -- etc etc
  monic := minpoly.monic (Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral α)

to help Lean out, you can "fix" defeqs by overriding fields:

/-- If `α` generates `S` as an algebra, then `S` is given by adjoining a root of `minpoly R α`. -/
def mkOfAdjoinEqTop'
    [Module.Finite R S] [Module.Free R S] [Nontrivial R]
    {α : S} (hα : Algebra.adjoin R {α} = ⊤) :
    IsAdjoinRootMonic S (minpoly R α) where
  __ : IsAdjoinRoot S (minpoly R α) :=
  let f := minpoly R α
  have hf := minpoly.monic (Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral (R := R) α)
  let φ : AdjoinRoot f →ₐ[R] S :=
      AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom f (Algebra.ofId R S) α (minpoly.aeval R α)
  haveI := hf.free_adjoinRoot; haveI := hf.finite_adjoinRoot
  IsAdjoinRoot.ofAdjoinRootEquiv <| AlgEquiv.ofBijective φ <| by
    have hφ : Function.Surjective φ := by
      rw [Algebra.adjoin_singleton_eq_range_aeval, AlgHom.range_eq_top] at hα
      intro s; obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hα s
      exact ⟨AdjoinRoot.mk f p, by simp [φ, ← aeval_def, hp]⟩
    sorry -- etc etc
  monic := minpoly.monic (Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral α)
  map := aeval α
